title: [PDF] Backflow Preventer Location for Secondary Protection - Phoenix
content: "POINT OF SERVICE DELIVERY" MEANS THE TERMINAL END OF A SERVICE CONNECTION FROM THE PUBLIC WATER SYSTEM. IF A METER IS INSTALLED AT THE END OF THE SERVICE CONNECTION, THEN THE POINT OF SERVICE DELIVERY SHALL MEAN THE DOWNSTREAM END (I.E., CUSTOMER'S SIDE) OF THE METER. IF AN UNMETERED CONNECTION EXISTS, THEN THE POINT OF SERVICE DELIVERY SHALL MEAN AT THE POINT OF DEMARCATION BETWEEN THE PUBLIC RIGHT-OF-WAY OR EASEMENTS AND PRIVATE PROPERTY.

title: Amendment to 2024 International Building Code (IBC)
content:
## Section 1803.5.13 — Post-tensioned slabs on ground

**Submitted by:** International Building Code Committee

### Code text

> **1803.5.13 Post-tensioned slabs on ground.**  
> A geotechnical investigation is required for the design of all structural post-tensioned slabs on ground. A geotechnical investigation is not required where the post-tensioning is added only for crack control with individual wall and column footings provided. Where required, the investigation report shall include all soil parameters as outlined in PTI DC-10.5. Information required on the drawings includes, but is not limited to, slab type, soil parameters, bearing value and depth, coefficient of subgrade friction, soil subgrade modulus, em and ym for expansive soils and all special inspection requirements.

### Stated reason

- Structural post-tensioned slabs on ground are complicated to design structurally.
- They can only be designed correctly with soil information from the specific construction site.

### Cost impact

- **Minimal cost impact.**
- A geotechnical investigation is required to complete these designs.

### Action dates

| 2024 Code Committee | 01/9/2024 |
| Development Advisory Board (DAB) Subcommittee | 02/27/2025 |
| Development Advisory Board (DAB) | 04/22/2025 |

| City Council Action | 06/18/2025 |

- Adopted by City of Phoenix Ordinance **G-7397**, effective **August 1, 2025**.

## Section 1907.2 — Nonstructural slabs-on-ground

**Submitted by:** International Building Code Committee

### Code text

> **1907.2 Nonstructural slabs-on-ground.**  
> Nonstructural slabs-on-ground shall be required to comply with Sections 1904.2, 1907.3, and 1907.4, and 1907.5. Portions of the nonstructural slabs-on-ground used to resist uplift forces or overturning shall be designed in accordance with accepted engineering practice throughout the entire portion designated as dead load to resist uplift forces or overturning.

### Stated reason

- Many structures have, and continue to be, constructed with post-tensioned slabs on ground.
- If a tendon is cut throughout the life of the structure, it can cause serious injury to people in the area.
- The amendment clarifies that permanent identification of such slabs is required for both structural and nonstructural slabs-on-ground.

### Cost impact

- **No cost impact.**

### Action dates

- Adopted by City of Phoenix Ordinance **G-7397**, effective **August 1, 2025**.

## Section 1907.5 — Permanent identification of post-tensioned slabs on ground

**Submitted by:** International Building Code Committee

### Code text

> **1907.5 Post-tensioned slabs on ground.**  
> All post-tensioned slabs on ground shall be permanently stamped, marked, or otherwise identified in a conspicuous location indicated the slab is a post-tensioned slab. Conspicuous locations include, but are not limited to, entrance porches, slabs at garage doors, or patio slabs.

### Stated reasons

- Many structures have been, and continue to be, constructed with post-tensioned slabs on ground.
- If a tendon is cut throughout the life of the structure, it can cause serious injury to people in the area.
- The stamp provides rapid identification that the slab is constructed with tendons.
- The contractor will know to identify tendon locations before cutting or drilling into the slab.

### Cost impact

- **No cost impact.**

## Related geotechnical-investigation provision — Section 1803.2

### Code text

> **1803.2 Investigation required.**  
> Geotechnical investigations shall be conducted in accordance with Section 1803.3 through 1803.5.

**Exceptions:**

1. The building official shall be permitted to waive the requirement for a geotechnical investigation where satisfactory data from adjacent areas is available that demonstrates an investigation is not necessary for any of the conditions in Section 1803.5.1 through 1803.5.6 and Section 1803.5.10 and 1803.5.11.
2. The building official shall be permitted to waive the requirement for a geotechnical investigation for lightweight or temporary structures where reasonable presumptive load bearing values are used.

### Stated reasons

- Phoenix has had a long-standing policy allowing the use of presumptive load-bearing soil values found elsewhere in the code instead of a full geotechnical investigation for some structures.
- Full geotechnical investigations can be a large financial burden for projects involving small-scale structures with low loads.
- The provision does not undo powers found elsewhere in the code for requiring a geotechnical investigation where the classification, strength, moisture sensitivity or compressibility of the soil is in doubt.
- The code compels a geotechnical investigation where the area is likely to have expansive soil.

### Cost impact

- **Minimal cost impact.**
- The amendment reduces construction costs for small projects by not requiring a full geotechnical investigation.
